text:
Predicates:
Hydrocarbon(x) ::: x is a hydrocarbon.
Organic(x) ::: x is an organic compound.
Chemical(x) ::: x is a chemical compound.
Alkane(x) ::: x is an alkane.
Contain(x, y) ::: x contains y.
Element(x) ::: x is an element.
Premises:
∀x (Hydrocarbon(x) → Organic(x)) ::: All hydrocarbons are organic compounds.
∀x (Alkane(x) → Hydrocarbon(x)) ::: All alkanes are hydrocarbons.
∀x (Organic(x) → Chemical(x)) ::: All organic compounds are chemical compounds.
∀x (Organic(x) → Contain(x, carbon)) ::: All organic compounds contain carbon.
∀x (Chemical(x) → ¬∃y (Element(y) ∧ ∀z (Contain(x, z) → z = y))) ::: No chemical compounds contain only one element.
(Chemical(mixture) ∧ ∃y (Element(y) ∧ ∀z (Contain(mixture, z) → z = y))) ⊕ ¬(Chemical(mixture) ∨ ∃y (Element(y) ∧ ∀z (Contain(mixture, z) → z = y))) ::: The mixture either both is a chemical compound and contains only one element, or neither.
Conclusion:
(Alkane(mixture) ∧ Contain(mixture, carbon)) ::: The mixture is an alkane and contains carbon.
